title: What Temperature Should a Freezer Be?

seo.title: What Temperature Should a Freezer Be?
seo.meta_description: Keep a freezer around 0°F (−18°C). Use an independent thermometer and check loading, the door seal, and settings if temperatures rise.
seo.search_intent: Know the correct freezer temperature and how to verify it when the display or food texture suggests the freezer may be too warm.

excerpt: The practical target is 0°F (−18°C). A control dial number is not always an actual temperature, so an independent freezer thermometer is useful.
content_html:
Set the freezer to maintain about 0°F (−18°C). That temperature keeps food frozen and provides some margin for normal door-opening fluctuations.

Measure instead of trusting a dial number

Controls labeled 1 through 5 often represent relative cooling, not degrees. Place a freezer thermometer in a representative area and give the appliance enough time to stabilize.

One reading is not the whole story

Opening the door or adding a large load can raise temperature temporarily. Look at the trend over several hours before repeatedly changing settings.

Frost and soft packages are clues

A poor door seal, blocked vents, or tightly packed food can create warm spots. Rearrange items without covering airflow openings and inspect the gasket.

Do not hide a malfunction with the coldest setting

If the freezer cannot reach 0°F despite good airflow, a closed door, and adequate stabilization time, service may be needed.

After a power outage or major thaw, the safety question becomes how warm food became and for how long, not simply where the thermostat is set.

faq.question: Is 0°F too cold?
faq.answer: No. It is the standard target for frozen-food storage.

faq.question: Where should I place a freezer thermometer?
faq.answer: Use a central, representative location rather than directly against an air outlet.

faq.question: Why does the display differ from my thermometer?
faq.answer: Sensor location and cooling cycles can cause differences; watch the trend and consult the manual if the gap persists.
